note: This unit's vocabulary is for questions that can't be settled by an experiment — the branches of philosophy, the structure of an argument, and a handful of famous positions.

examples.de: Die Philosophie stellt Fragen, die sich nicht empirisch beantworten lassen.
examples.en: Philosophy asks questions that cannot be answered empirically.

note: The branch of philosophy asking about the fundamental nature of reality, beyond what can be directly observed.

examples.de: Die Metaphysik fragt nach dem Wesen der Wirklichkeit jenseits des sinnlich Erfahrbaren.
examples.en: Metaphysics asks about the nature of reality beyond what can be sensorily experienced.

note: The branch of philosophy examining what knowledge is, what we can know, and how we come to know it.

examples.de: Die Erkenntnistheorie untersucht, was wir wissen können und woher dieses Wissen stammt.
examples.en: Epistemology examines what we can know and where that knowledge comes from.

note: The branch of philosophy examining what counts as right action — distinct from the applied, case-specific medizinethik (B2).

examples.de: Die Ethik beschäftigt sich mit der Frage, was richtiges Handeln ausmacht.
examples.en: Ethics deals with the question of what constitutes right action.

note: The branch of metaphysics asking what it means for something to exist at all, and what kinds of things exist.

examples.de: Die Ontologie untersucht, was es überhaupt bedeutet, dass etwas existiert.
examples.en: Ontology examines what it even means for something to exist.

note: The fact or state of being — a central concept in 20th-century existentialist philosophy.

examples.de: Die menschliche Existenz war ein zentrales Thema der Philosophie des 20. Jahrhunderts.
examples.en: Human existence was a central theme of 20th-century philosophy.

note: The faculty of rational thought — central to Enlightenment philosophy's trust in human reasoning.

examples.de: Die Aufklärung setzte großes Vertrauen in die menschliche Vernunft.
examples.en: The Enlightenment placed great trust in human reason.

note: Acting or reasoning according to logic and evidence — the adjective form is rational.

examples.de: Nicht jede Entscheidung folgt strikt der Rationalität.
examples.en: Not every decision strictly follows rationality.

note: A starting statement an argument builds on — an argument's conclusion is only as reliable as its premises.

examples.de: Ein Argument ist nur so stark wie seine Prämissen.
examples.en: An argument is only as strong as its premises.

note: What necessarily follows from a set of premises — distinct from Fazit (C1 Textkohäsion unit), which is an essay's closing verdict rather than a logical step.

examples.de: Aus diesen Prämissen ergibt sich zwingend eine bestimmte Schlussfolgerung.
examples.en: From these premises, a certain conclusion necessarily follows.

note: A formal argument with two premises and a conclusion — the classic example: all humans are mortal; Socrates is human; therefore Socrates is mortal.

examples.de: Ein klassischer Syllogismus: Alle Menschen sind sterblich; Sokrates ist ein Mensch; also ist Sokrates sterblich.
examples.en: A classic syllogism: all humans are mortal; Socrates is human; therefore Socrates is mortal.

note: A statement accepted as true without proof, used as the starting point for further reasoning.

examples.de: Ein Axiom wird als wahr vorausgesetzt, ohne selbst bewiesen zu werden.
examples.en: An axiom is assumed to be true without being proven itself.

note: A method of reasoning through opposition: a thesis is met by its antithesis, and the tension resolves into a synthesis.

examples.de: Die Dialektik beschreibt den Fortschritt des Denkens durch These, Antithese und Synthese.
examples.en: Dialectic describes the progress of thought through thesis, antithesis, and synthesis.

note: A statement or situation that seems to contradict itself, yet may still contain a deeper truth.

examples.de: Ein Paradoxon scheint sich selbst zu widersprechen und ist doch nicht einfach falsch.
examples.en: A paradox seems to contradict itself, yet isn't simply false.

note: A hypothetical scenario used to test a theory or intuition without a real experiment — trolley problems and similar dilemmas are classic examples.

examples.de: Ein Gedankenexperiment prüft eine Theorie, ohne dass ein echtes Experiment nötig wäre.
examples.en: A thought experiment tests a theory without an actual experiment being necessary.

note: The position that every event is fixed by prior causes, leaving no room for genuine chance or choice.

examples.de: Der Determinismus geht davon aus, dass jedes Ereignis durch vorherige Ursachen festgelegt ist.
examples.en: Determinism assumes that every event is determined by prior causes.

note: The capacity to choose otherwise than one did — its compatibility with determinism is a classic philosophical dispute.

examples.de: Ob der Mensch einen freien Willen hat, wird seit Jahrhunderten diskutiert.
examples.en: Whether humans have free will has been discussed for centuries.

note: An ethical position judging actions by their consequences — specifically, the overall benefit they produce for the greatest number.

examples.de: Der Utilitarismus bewertet Handlungen nach ihrem Nutzen für die größte Zahl an Menschen.
examples.en: Utilitarianism evaluates actions by their benefit for the greatest number of people.

note: Kant's principle that one should act only according to a rule one could will to become a universal law — an ethics of duty rather than consequences.

examples.de: Kants kategorischer Imperativ verlangt, nur nach Maximen zu handeln, die man als allgemeines Gesetz wollen könnte.
examples.en: Kant's categorical imperative demands acting only according to maxims one could will to become universal law.

note: A philosophical position that fundamentally questions whether certain knowledge is possible at all.

examples.de: Der Skeptizismus zweifelt grundsätzlich an der Möglichkeit sicheren Wissens.
examples.en: Skepticism fundamentally doubts the possibility of certain knowledge.

note: The position that truth or value depends on perspective, rather than being universal and absolute.

examples.de: Der Relativismus bestreitet, dass es eine einzige, universell gültige Wahrheit gibt.
examples.en: Relativism disputes that there is a single, universally valid truth.

note: What a claim has when it accurately reflects reality — a concept philosophers have debated since antiquity.

examples.de: Über den Begriff der Wahrheit streiten Philosophen seit der Antike.
examples.en: Philosophers have argued about the concept of truth since antiquity.

note: The quality of depending on an individual's perspective, feelings, or experience.

examples.de: Die Subjektivität der Wahrnehmung erschwert eine objektive Bewertung.
examples.en: The subjectivity of perception makes an objective assessment difficult.

note: The quality of being independent of individual perspective — an ideal many fields aim for without ever fully reaching it.

examples.de: Völlige Objektivität ist in den Geisteswissenschaften kaum zu erreichen.
examples.en: Complete objectivity is hardly achievable in the humanities.

note: Describes a judgment or description that doesn't depend on personal perspective or preference.

examples.de: Ein objektives Urteil berücksichtigt keine persönlichen Vorlieben.
examples.en: An objective judgment takes no personal preferences into account.

note: Describes something shaped by an individual's own perspective, feelings, or experience.

examples.de: Geschmack ist immer subjektiv.
examples.en: Taste is always subjective.

note: Describes an argument or system with no internal contradictions — a basic requirement for sound reasoning.

examples.de: Eine gute Argumentation sollte in sich widerspruchsfrei sein.
examples.en: Good argumentation should be internally free of contradiction.

note: Something taken to be true without being explicitly stated or proven — more everyday than the formal Prämisse, but functionally similar.

examples.de: Die gesamte Theorie beruht auf einer einzigen, unbewiesenen Annahme.
examples.en: The entire theory rests on a single, unproven assumption.
